reconcile.note: Gill argues Matthew's transition markers mark the true chronological order, while Luke's arrangement narrates events without regard to sequence, so no real contradiction results.

discrepancy.note: Strauss, following Schleiermacher, holds Matthew's climactic order original and judges Luke's swapped sequence a later, unhappy rearrangement.

quotes.text: Matthew's order seems to be the original, because it is founded on the relative importance of the temptations, which is the main consideration,—the invitation to worship Satan, which is the strongest temptation, being made the final one; whereas the arrangement of Luke looks like a later and not very happy transposition
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), pt. II, ch. on the temptation of Jesus, on Matthew 4:5 and Luke 4:5.
